## Project Overview

**travel-assist** is a Spring Boot (Kotlin) REST API for managing travel trips. It exposes a standard CRUD interface at `/api/trips`, backed by Spring Data JPA with an H2 in-memory database. The application is structured using the classic Controller → Service → Repository layered architecture and is modularised with Spring Modulith.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Primary language | Kotlin |
| Framework | Spring Boot 4.0.4 |
| Persistence | Spring Data JPA + H2 (in-memory) |
| Build system | Gradle (Kotlin DSL — `build.gradle.kts`) |
| Entry point | `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/TravelAssistApplication.kt` |
| Modularity | Spring Modulith |
| Containerisation | Docker Compose (spring-boot-docker-compose, local dev only) |
| Native image | GraalVM Native Image plugin configured |

## Commands

Use these exact commands. Do not invent alternatives (e.g. `mvn`, `npm`, `make`).

```bash
# Resolve and download all dependencies
./gradlew dependencies

# Compile and package the application (runs tests as part of the build)
./gradlew build

# Run all tests only
./gradlew test

# Start the application locally (H2 in-memory, no external DB required)
./gradlew bootRun
```

> **No lint command is configured** in this project. Do not add or assume one.
>
> **Native compilation** is available via the GraalVM plugin but is NOT a routine command — do not invoke `./gradlew nativeCompile` unless explicitly instructed, as it has known compatibility constraints (see Pitfalls).

## Safe Operations

The following are explicitly permitted for agent-driven changes. Stay within these boundaries.

- **Add new REST endpoints** inside existing controllers (e.g., `TripController`) or in new controller classes under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/controller/`.
- **Add new service methods** to `TripService` or create new service classes under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/service/`.
- **Add new DTOs** under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/`. Remember to use `@field:` annotation use-site targets for Jakarta validation (see Pitfalls).
- **Add new JPA entity classes** under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/`, following the pattern established in `Trip.kt` (`var` fields, nullable id with `GenerationType.IDENTITY`).
- **Add new repository interfaces** under `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/repository/`, extending `JpaRepository` or equivalent Spring Data interfaces.
- **Add or modify unit and integration tests** under `src/test/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/`. JUnit 5 is the test framework — use it exclusively.
- **Modify non-secret application configuration** in `src/main/resources/application.properties` or `src/main/resources/application.yml`. Be aware both files exist and are loaded simultaneously (see Pitfalls).
- **Add new dependencies** to `build.gradle.kts` when a task genuinely requires a new library.

## Domain Glossary

Understand these concepts before modifying any business logic.

### Trip
The central entity of this application. A `Trip` is a JPA-managed object persisted in the `trips` database table. It represents a single travel trip and carries:
- `id` — auto-generated primary key (`GenerationType.IDENTITY`), nullable until persisted.
- `title` — the name of the trip.
- `description` — optional free-text description.
- `destination` — where the trip goes.
- Date range fields — start and end dates of the trip.

All fields are declared as `var` (mutable) — this is intentional for JPA compatibility with Kotlin data classes.

### TripDto
A data transfer object used exclusively for inbound HTTP requests (create and update operations). It is **not** a JPA entity. It carries the same logical fields as `Trip` but enforces input validation via Jakarta Bean Validation annotations. Critically: annotations must use the `@field:` use-site target (e.g., `@field:NotBlank`) so the constraint is placed on the backing field rather than the constructor parameter — omitting `field:` silently breaks validation.

### TripService
The transactional business-logic layer sitting between the controller and the repository. All database-mutating operations (`create`, `update`, `delete`) are wrapped in Spring `@Transactional` boundaries here. New business rules belong in this class (or a new service class following the same pattern).

### TripRepository
A Spring Data JPA repository interface for `Trip`. It inherits standard CRUD methods (`save`, `findById`, `findAll`, `deleteById`, etc.) from `JpaRepository` — no custom queries are needed for basic operations. If you need custom queries, add them here using Spring Data derived method names or `@Query`.

### TripController
The HTTP entry point. It maps incoming REST requests at the `/api/trips` base path to `TripService` methods:
- `GET /api/trips` — list all trips.
- `GET /api/trips/{id}` — get a single trip by id.
- `POST /api/trips` — create a new trip (body: `TripDto`).
- `PUT /api/trips/{id}` — update an existing trip (body: `TripDto`).
- `DELETE /api/trips/{id}` — delete a trip.

The controller is responsible only for HTTP concerns (status codes, request/response mapping). Business logic must not live here.

| `Trip` | `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/model/Trip.kt` | JPA entity mapped to the `trips` table. Core domain object with id, title, description, destination, and date fields. |
| `TripDto` | `src/main/kotlin/com/vb/nattamai/travelassist/dto/TripDto.kt` | Inbound request DTO with Jakarta validation constraints. Used for POST and PUT request bodies — never used as a JPA entity. |

## Potential Pitfalls

Read these before writing any code. Each one represents a real risk of silent failure or a broken build.

---

### ⚠️ Spring Boot 4.0.4 is bleeding-edge
This project targets Spring Boot 4.0.4, which is a very recent release. Third-party libraries and Gradle plugins may not yet declare compatibility with it. Before adding any new dependency, verify it explicitly supports Spring Boot 4.x. Do not assume Spring Boot 3.x documentation applies without checking for breaking changes.

---

### ⚠️ Kotlin data classes as JPA entities require `var` and nullable `id`
The `Trip` entity is a Kotlin class (not a data class, but Kotlin-idiomatic) using `var` for all mutable fields and a **nullable `id`** with `GenerationType.IDENTITY`. This is intentional. Do not refactor fields to `val` — JPA requires mutability for managed entities. Do not make `id` non-nullable — it is `null` before the entity is first persisted.

---

### ⚠️ DGS Codegen plugin is configured but has no GraphQL schemas yet
The Netflix DGS Codegen Gradle plugin is declared in `build.gradle.kts` and looks for schema files under `src/main/resources/graphql-client/`. **That directory and its schemas do not exist yet.** If the `generateJava` task is invoked (e.g. as a dependency of another task), it may fail. Do not invoke DGS codegen tasks unless you are explicitly adding GraphQL schema files as part of your task.

---

### ⚠️ Both `application.properties` and `application.yml` exist simultaneously
Spring Boot loads **both** `src/main/resources/application.properties` and `src/main/resources/application.yml`. When the same property key appears in both files, the resolution order can produce unexpected overrides. When adding or changing configuration, check both files to avoid silent conflicts. Prefer consolidating into one file when possible, but do not delete either without verifying no unique properties will be lost.

---

### ⚠️ Jakarta validation in Kotlin DTOs requires the `@field:` use-site target
In `TripDto`, validation annotations must be written as `@field:NotBlank`, `@field:NotNull`, etc. — **not** `@NotBlank` or `@NotNull` alone. Without the `field:` use-site target, Kotlin places the annotation on the constructor parameter rather than the backing field, and the Jakarta validation framework (which inspects fields) will silently ignore the constraint. The `TitleDto` already demonstrates the correct pattern — follow it exactly.

---

### ⚠️ GraalVM Native Image has reflection and proxy constraints
The GraalVM native image plugin is configured in this project. Native compilation imposes strict constraints: dynamic proxies, reflection, and runtime class scanning (all heavily used by Spring, JPA, and Kotlin) require explicit native hints or `reflect-config.json` entries.
